Add a rule that tells owners and admins when events or money look wrong. What it watches is its
kind:

  event_count       The event happened --threshold times in the window,
                    to at least --min-people people.
  failure_share     More than --threshold (0 to 1) of the attempts in the
                    window failed. An attempt is --event, the failure, or
                    --success-event.
  volume_drop       The event fell by --threshold (0 to 1) against the same
                    window in the weeks before.
  metric_threshold  The --metric over the window is --direction above or
                    below --threshold: money as you write it (5000 for
                    5,000.00) in --currency, the organization's reporting
                    currency unless named, which the alert keeps; counts as
                    whole numbers. MRR and active subscriptions or trials are
                    read as they stand, with --window-hours 24.
  metric_change     The --metric moved by --threshold (0.1 for 10%),
                    --direction up, down or either, against the window
                    before; a day of a flow such as revenue against the
                    same day a week earlier.

A metric alert's window is 24, 168 or 720 hours, and --filter narrows it,
as dimension=values or dimension!=values: store=apple-app-store,
country!=US,CA, trait:plan=pro. It is first checked at the next quarter past
the hour. On a terminal, what is not passed is asked for.

Usage:
  voidhash analytics alerts create [flags]

Flags:
      --basis <gross|net_of_tax|proceeds>
                                   For a money metric: what its amounts count (default: the metric's
                                   own)
      --currency <code>            For a money metric: the ISO 4217 code its threshold is in, such
                                   as EUR (default: the organization's reporting currency)
      --direction <above|below|up|down|either>
                                   For a metric alert: above or below for metric_threshold, up, down
                                   or either for metric_change
      --event <event>              The event to watch; for failure_share, the event of a failed
                                   attempt
      --filter <dimension=values>  For a metric alert: narrows it, as dimension=values or
                                   dimension!=values; repeat for more (can be repeated)
  -h, --help                       Show help for this command
      --json                       Print the API object as JSON, for scripts
      --kind <event_count|failure_share|volume_drop|metric_threshold|metric_change>
                                   What it watches: too many of an event, too many failures among
                                   attempts, an event that fell against earlier weeks, a metric past
                                   a value, or a metric that moved
      --metric <mrr|revenue|refunds|new_mrr|expansion_mrr|reactivation_mrr|contraction_mrr|churned_mrr|net_new_mrr|active_subscriptions|new_subscriptions|churned_subscriptions|paying_customers|active_trials|new_trials|trial_conversions>
                                   For a metric alert: the built-in metric to watch
      --min-people <people>        For event_count: distinct people it must affect (default: 2). Use
                                   1 when one person matters
      --name <name>                What a person reads in the notice
      --project <project>          Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name
                                   (default: this directory's project, then your default project)
      --success-event <event>      For failure_share: the event of an attempt that worked
      --threshold <threshold>      For event_count, the count that fires it; for failure_share and
                                   volume_drop, a share from 0 to 1; for metric_threshold, the
                                   metric's value, money as written (5000 for 5,000.00); for
                                   metric_change, a share such as 0.1
      --window-hours <hours>       The trailing window each hourly check reads, in hours: 1, 6, 24
                                   or 168 for an event, 24, 168 or 720 for a metric

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash analytics alerts create --name "Checkout errors" --kind event_count --event checkout_error --window-hours 1 --threshold 20
  voidhash analytics alerts create --name "Payments failing" --kind failure_share --event payment_failed --success-event payment_succeeded --window-hours 6 --threshold 0.3
  voidhash analytics alerts create --name "Signups dropped" --kind volume_drop --event signup --window-hours 24 --threshold 0.5
  voidhash analytics alerts create --name "App Store MRR falling" --kind metric_change --metric mrr --filter store=apple-app-store --direction down --window-hours 720 --threshold 0.1
  voidhash analytics alerts create --name "Refunds abroad" --kind metric_threshold --metric refunds --filter country!=US --direction above --window-hours 168 --threshold 500
